newsitem.title: UK: BZW details senior management shake-up.
newsitem.headline: BZW details senior management shake-up.

text.p: BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays Plc, on Thursday detailed changes to its senior management team.
Donald Brydon, who had been acting chief executive for the last six months, has agreed to leave the firm, BZW said in a statement.
Bill Harrison, formerly of merchant bank Robert Fleming, was appointed as chief executive of the group in June to replace BZW head David Band, who died suddenly in March.
BZW said Jonathan Davie had stepped down as chief executive of equities, having already said he wanted to do so at the end of the remuneration round in February 1997.

"It has been agreed that this date be brought forward and that Steve Harker, his current deputy, becomes the chief executive of equities and a member of the management committee with immediate effect," the company added.
Davie has been made full-time deputy chairman of BZW.
Patrick O'Sullivan has been appointed chief operating officer and will join the management committee. O'Sullivan is currently chief executive of structured finance.

BZW said Bob Diamond, who joined in July as chief executive of its global markets division, had joined the management committee along with David Cannon, finance director, and Sally Bott, head of Human Resources.
Harrison said he had "decided to strengthen the senior management team and bring additional skills and experience on to the management committee".

He said Brydon, who joined the Barclays group in 1977, "has served BZW and the group well in building the asset management business and also during the last six months in his role as acting chief executive. We wish him well for the future".
Brydon, who had been Band's deputy before his death, said BZW was in good shape and had "a vigorous new management team to take it forward in the next stage of its development".
At the time of the announcement of Harrison's appointment in June, BZW had said Brydon would remain as deputy chief executive when Harrison took over.
